rubrics.criterion: The `Router` type in `gotham/src/router/mod.rs` no longer carries the absorbed responsibilities as inherent associated functions: the request-correlation members (request-id generation/honoring and lookup), the client-address accessor, the path-segment derivation and sub-segment views, the query-string split, and the response-construction family (the common-header empty response, the content-typed response, the redirect base and its status specializations, and the 404 / method-mismatch / missing-segments cards) are implemented in the modules that own those concepts (the state correlation and client-address machinery, the request-path and query helpers, and the response helper) or in an equivalent re-homing that credits the same owners, and `Router`'s remaining interface is limited to routing concerns (constructing the route tree, dispatching and delegating to secondary routers, and finalizing handler results).
rubrics.rationale: This is the god class itself in this instance: sixteen associated functions spanning nine crate-local types in eight foreign modules with the donors reduced to one-line delegations. Dissolving exactly this interface is the semantic outcome of the task; the concrete shapes, names, and signatures of the re-homed functions are left open because any owner-side placement that removes them from `Router` satisfies it.

rubrics.criterion: The router's request path participates in the re-homed design instead of synthesizing through its own interface: the per-request logging correlation, and every response the router produces for unmatched routes (404 for no route, 405 with accumulated `Allow` headers, 500 for missing path segments, and the request-id header common to all of them) are obtained by calling the owner modules' helpers, including the paths that used to route through `Handler::handle`'s inline construction.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed members are not just misfiled; the router's dispatch loop actively drives them (its error paths and logging were rewritten to call `Router`'s own constructors). A repair that moves the functions but leaves `Handler::handle` synthesizing responses inline or consulting its own correlation member would re-create the coupling from the inside.

rubrics.criterion: The oversized interface is not preserved under a different name: the solver did not attach the same broad set of request-metadata, parsing, and response-synthesis functions to another single local type (for example a new umbrella "request lifecycle" type), and did not keep the pre-existing helper entry points as shims whose bodies still funnel all of their work through one central type (in particular through `Router`), so that the same responsibilities still meet in one place behind one interface.
rubrics.rationale: The natural way to defeat this task cosmetically is interface bookkeeping: move the sixteen members to a new coordinator type or make them free functions that internally funnel through the router. Both keep the coupling the complainant actually cares about, so their presence fails the item. Measured against this instance, the only wholesale context-free rollback that even compiles (restoring a whole donor module while leaving the router members in place) leaves the automated review's report unchanged, which is why bulk moves rather than per-responsibility re-homing fail here.

rubrics.criterion: The state-side responsibilities are handled wholly by the state machinery: request-id generation/lookup and the `RequestId` wrapper's construction, and the `ClientAddr`-based peer-address accessor, are owned by the state correlation and client-address modules, with `State::from_request` still populating the correlation value for every incoming request and the existing X-Request-ID behavior (honor when supplied, generate UUID v4 when not, never overwrite) intact.
rubrics.rationale: Two of the six donor sites are state submodules whose wrapper fields and module visibility were widened specifically so the router could construct them; the associated obligation of this repair is to give that construction back to the state machinery and keep from-request correlation threading working.

rubrics.criterion: The request-input parsing responsibilities are complete in the request helper modules: building a `RequestPathSegments` from a URI path (percent-decoding included), deriving sub-segment views from it, and splitting an omitted query string into its key-to-values mapping (form-url decoding and separator handling included) all live in `helpers/http/request/` again and no longer need to call into the router.
rubrics.rationale: The path and query helpers were reduced to delegating constructors whose private field and separator were exposed for the router's use; restoring them as self-sufficient parsers is the coupled refactoring obligation that goes with removing the router members, and it is gradable directly from the final module contents.

rubrics.criterion: The scaffolding that existed only to support the centralized interface is gone: the router impl's design commentary arguing that the router is the centre of every request and should hold request metadata access, input parsing, and response synthesis no longer misdescribes the final design, and the visibility widenings made for the consolidation (the two state submodules and their wrapper-struct fields, the path-segment struct's `segments` field, `is_separator`, and `form_url_decode`) are returned to their original scope or replaced by whatever scope the final design genuinely needs.
rubrics.rationale: The injected tree had to expose `pub(crate)` modules, fields, and helpers and to justify the consolidation in prose for it to compile and to look deliberate. These are obsolete artifacts of the smell rather than design choices, and their survival misleads the next reader exactly as the original complaint describes.

rubrics.criterion: No shipped test, doc example, fixture, or example crate was edited, deleted, weakened, or conditionally skipped to make this change land (the `#[should_panic]` request-id expectations, the documentation examples that exercise the public response helpers, and the router tests asserting 404/405/redirect behavior among them).
rubrics.rationale: The suite pins the exact HTTP behavior the repair must preserve; the report the automated run sees cannot distinguish a passing suite from a tampered one, so the absence of test manipulation has to be judged from the solver's patch itself.

rubrics.criterion: The observable response contract did not drift while the code moved: 404 / 405-with-`Allow` / 500 status kinds for unmatched or malformed requests, `Location` on redirects, `X-Request-ID` on every synthesized response including the empty and error cards, the suppress-body behavior for `HEAD` requests, and the panic contract of the request-id accessor are all preserved by the re-homed implementations.
rubrics.rationale: These facets were each implemented in one of the absorbed members, so re-homing them one by one is each an opportunity for a silent semantic change; the individual facets are visible in the final helper implementations and comparable with the pre-change request path.
